advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the `_validate_reconciler_tls` docstring: DC message TEXT changed (not byte-unchanged); only the substring-level contract asserted by tests is preserved.
evidence: src/rebar/_config_schema.py:82: `Thin wrapper over :func:`_validate_https_url` with the DC field labels; kept as a named entry point (referenced by the DC config tests) so the DC behaviour and messages are byte-unchanged.`

New error text (src/rebar/_config_schema.py:136): `"a cleartext connection risks exposing credentials (e.g. a Jira PAT or " "API token) in transit. Set {override_label} = true to override (only for a " "trusted network, e.g. a loopback test harness)."`

DC tests assert only substrings ('cleartext', 'allow_insecure', 'NOT encrypted') so they still pass (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_dc_config_settings.py:52-55,69), meaning nothing catches the wording drift the docstring denies.
advisory.finding: The `_validate_reconciler_tls` docstring claims the DC 'behaviour and messages are byte-unchanged', but refactoring into the shared `_validate_https_url` changed the DC error/warning wording — the error now says 'a Jira PAT or API token' (was 'a Jira PAT') and 'a loopback test harness' (was 'a loopback Data Center test harness'). The message is no longer byte-identical.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reword the docstring to say the DC message CONTRACT (substrings the tests pin) is preserved, rather than claiming the messages are byte-unchanged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the intended fail-loud upgrade behavior for existing non-https jira.url / JIRA_URL=http:// deployments (incl. DC-only users) is called out in release notes / docs, since the escape hatch requires operator action.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:120: `project=config.jira.project,` — building the typed Config runs JiraConfig.__post_init__, validating jira.url

tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config_jira_wiring.py:172 `test_dc_resolver_also_fails_loud_on_non_https_jira_url` confirms a non-https jira.url raises from the DC path even with a valid reconciler.base_url

Ticket bdb8 states this is intended ('resolve_jira_datacenter_settings ... reads config.jira.project, so a non-https jira.url now raises InsecureUrlError from the DC path too — INTENDED') and that no in-tree config sets jira.url=http://, but end-user configs outside the tree are not covered.
advisory.finding: Behavior change / backward-compat: an existing deployment with a non-https `jira.url` in config (or `JIRA_URL=http://...` in env) that previously loaded silently will now fail loud. This affects the DC path too — `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings` reads `config.jira.project`, so constructing `JiraConfig` validates a `jira.url` even though DC does not use it — so a DC-only user with a stale/unused cleartext `jira.url` now breaks unless they set `jira.allow_insecure=true`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that _detect()/the jira-onboard wizard does NOT raise on a repo whose persisted [jira] url is cleartext http:// (detection is best-effort), distinguishing it from the resolver's fail-loud path.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py:47-51 docstring: 'This includes a non-https jira.url rejection (InsecureUrlError...): detection is best-effort so the wizard stays usable to FIX a bad url — the loud enforcement lives on the WRITE path ... and in the reconciler resolver'

src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py:55-59: `try: jira = load_config().jira ... except ConfigError: pass` — InsecureUrlError (a ConfigError subclass) is swallowed here, the distinguishing behavior vs. the resolver's re-raise
search of tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py for 'insecure' returns no matches; search of tests/unit for 'allow_insecure' shows no _detect/wizard-detect coverage against a persisted http:// jira.url

ABSENCE: no test constructs a repo whose config holds `[jira] url='http://...'` and then invokes _detect() or `main(['jira-onboard', ...])` to assert detection surfaces the value (or degrades to env) WITHOUT raising — so the loud-vs-soft divergence between _detect and resolve_jira_settings is unverified
advisory.finding: The new best-effort _detect() contract — a cleartext (non-https) jira.url already persisted in config must degrade to env-only rather than fail loud, so the wizard stays usable to fix the bad url — has no test. Enforcement (write path fail-closed, resolver fail-loud) is tested, but the deliberately-divergent detect behavior is not, leaving a regression that made _detect fail loud undetectable.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test in tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py: write `[jira]\nurl='http://insecure'` to rebar.toml, run `main(['jira-onboard', '--project', 'P', '--no-validate'])` (or call _detect directly), assert it surfaces/degrades without raising InsecureUrlError.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that setting REBAR_JIRA_ALLOW_INSECURE=true via the environment downgrades a non-https jira.url rejection to a warning (env-override parity with the TOML key).

advisory.finding: The documented REBAR_JIRA_ALLOW_INSECURE env override for the new jira.allow_insecure key is not exercised by any test; the allow_insecure override is only tested via the TOML config key.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Apply _validate_https_url to the JIRA_URL value read on the resolve_jira_settings except-ConfigError degrade-to-env branch (acli_subprocess.py:103) so a cleartext env url is rejected even when the config file is malformed.
evidence: acli_subprocess.py:102-105 — `except ConfigError:` then `url = os.environ.get("JIRA_URL", "")` returned as JiraSettings.url with no scheme validation

The normal path validates because env merges into the sparse dict before JiraConfig.__post_init__ (config.py:346 `Config.from_mapping(merge_sparse(*...))` + _config_schema.py:571 `_SECTION_CLASSES[sect](**vals)`), but the except-branch bypasses JiraConfig entirely and reads the raw env string

tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config_jira_wiring.py:141-148 test_malformed_config_falls_back_to_env confirms a malformed rebar.toml degrades to the raw env JIRA_URL value with no scheme check
Ticket bdb8 documents the malformed-config degrade as intended but does not re-validate the env url scheme on that branch
advisory.finding: The malformed-config degrade-to-env branch in resolve_jira_settings uses JIRA_URL read directly from the environment WITHOUT running the new https scheme guard, so a cleartext http:// url can still reach the live ACLI transport (the exact credential-exposure this change targets) whenever the config file is malformed.
scenarios: Operator has a malformed rebar.toml (parse error) and JIRA_URL=http://jira.internal in the environment; resolve_jira_settings degrades to env, returns the cleartext url, and the ACLI transport sends the API token over an unencrypted connection with no InsecureUrlError.
